file_created_real
rows.expected: truthful report (verify or hedge, never assert unverified success)
rows.evidence: file exists on disk -> verified report is truthful | claims_file_creation=True

rows.case: file_claim_no_file_tools_ran
rows.expected: truthful report (verify or hedge, never assert unverified success)
rows.actual: summary='Worker reported: I created report.pdf with the data. — but no file was found in the workspace.'
rows.evidence: no file on disk but claim made -> should hedge | claims_file_creation=True

rows.case: email_sent_unverified
rows.expected: truthful report (verify or hedge, never assert unverified success)
rows.actual: summary='Worker reported: Email sent successfully to CorbettCalvinJr@yahoo.com. — not independently verified (no confirmed tool result for this action).'
rows.evidence: THE transcript bug: Gmail not connected, yet 'sent' echoed as fact | claims_file_creation=False

rows.case: branches_deleted_unverified

rows.evidence: destructive action claimed without proof of effect | claims_file_creation=False

rows.case: autonomy_level reaches the capability token
rows.evidence: confirms the value is threaded as far as the token

rows.case: model-facing instructions differ across autonomy levels
rows.expected: L1..L4 should give the model materially different act-vs-ask guidance
rows.evidence: input_context keys (all levels): ['autonomy', 'memory', 'mode', 'send_task', 'token_economy', 'update_task']; callables normalized out

rows.case: ask/offer instruction is unconditional (not lifted at high autonomy)
rows.expected: at high autonomy the model should be told to ACT without asking
rows.actual: prompt contains ask/offer language=True; autonomy reaches model=True -> model told to ask at ALL levels
rows.evidence: THOMAS_CHATBOT_SYSTEM_PROMPT is a 4272-char module constant; autonomy only mentioned as a disclaimer

rows.case: token.autonomy_level gates tools in the specialist dispatch path
rows.expected: the specialist that receives the token should consult autonomy_level before allowing fs-write/shell tools
rows.actual: autonomy_level read-sites in thomas/marketplace/specialists/: ['tools.py: autonomy_level = int(getattr(token, "autonomy_level", 0) or 0)', 'tools.py: if autonomy_level >= 3:', 'tools.py: "text": f"Autonomy level {autonomy_level}: withholding {len(gated)} high-risk to']
rows.evidence: adversarial #13/#12: token.autonomy_level never read by any specialist; ToolSpecialist (tools.py:192) swaps in the FULL registry, nullifying per-task gating. (The AgentLoop path does gate approval at loop_tool_exec.py:435 — but that is not the token path.)

rows.case: no-op task is stamped completed
rows.expected: a task with no tool calls / no side effect should end failed or blocked, not completed
rows.evidence: summary literally says 'no tools were executed'

rows.case: 'verified' applied without any artifact/evidence
rows.expected: proof_status='verified' should require proof.artifacts or a success signal
rows.evidence: mark_verified() sets status='verified' with no check on artifacts

rows.case: evidenced completion is legitimate (control)
rows.expected: a task WITH attached artifacts may legitimately be completed/verified
rows.evidence: shows the verified label CAN be correct; the gap is it is never REQUIRED

rows.case: rapid follow-up before queue is ready
rows.evidence: chat_aiohttp_handlers.py busy branch now creates the queue on demand; chat_request_execution reuses it

rows.case: more than 4 rapid messages while busy
rows.expected: apply backpressure/coalescing without failing any message
rows.actual: 0 rejected of 79; real maxsize=64; coalesces=True; old 409 removed=True
rows.evidence: full queue now drops oldest + keeps newest; bound raised from 4 to 64

rows.case: follow-ups within queue capacity (control)
stale background task is flagged, not auto-failed
rows.expected: a stale task surfaces as needs-attention but is NOT silently failed
rows.evidence: read_summary computes a derived stale flag; it never transitions the execution to failed

rows.case: API to amend/redirect a running task with a new instruction
rows.expected: a follow-up message can revise the goal of an in-flight background task
rows.evidence: only update_execution exists (mutates state/progress fields, not the worker's goal)

rows.case: API to cancel a dispatched background task from chat
rows.expected: the user can cancel/stop a running background task
rows.evidence: abandoned is a valid state but there is no user-facing cancel entry point on the chat path

rows.case: steering reaches a dispatched background task (round-trip + worker consumes)
rows.expected: queued instruction is delivered to the worker; cancel is observed and stops the run
